articles.title: Updating our Bengals preseason predictions. How we see 2026 finishing
articles.summary: Before the season, each of our Bengals experts predicted the team would win a playoff game. One of our reporters no longer feels that way.
articles.body:
Ja'Marr Chase, Bengals human highlight reel, through the years

The NFL season isn't going how we expected for the Cincinnati Bengals .

Now, to be fair, Cincinnati's 3-2 record going into the Week 6 bye is exactly what The Enquirer's two Bengals beat reporters and columnist all projected . But how the Bengals got there? Yeah, none of us can claim we had the team getting to 3-2 in the manner it did.

And going forward? Sheesh. At the very least, there are some doubts about what comes next in 2026. Collectively, our year-end predictions for the Bengals landed in a tight spread: Two of us projected 11-6 seasons with an AFC North championship, while columnist Jason Williams foresaw a 10-7 season with a Wild Card berth (and we all had Cincinnati winning a playoff game to advance to the Divisional round of AFC playoff bracket).

With the knowledge we have after five games − the running game is middling and inconsistent, the team lost two winnable games, and the worst team in the NFL had its best day offensively against Cincinnati, to name a few findings − this is my re-pick of the game-by-game predictions. And you better believe I'm backing off my 11-6 prediction.

Week 7: Bengals at Baltimore Ravens, 1 p.m., Oct. 25, CBS

Updated outlook: I said before the season that this would be the toughest divisional game for the Bengals in 2026. I still think that's correct. I think it's also still fair to say Cincinnati will benefit from two weeks of preparation for this game (they'll need it). You also have to consider that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is banged up. That would seem to benefit Cincinnati, except that Baltimore just beat the better-than-anticipated Atlanta Falcons with longtime quarterback and backup Tyler Huntley. Bottom line: If a terrible, 0-5 Dolphins team with a woeful Malik Willis at quarterback can have its best offensive day of the year against the Bengals defense, what's the serviceable Huntley and the gargantuan Derrick Henry going to do to Cincinnati? I'm flipping my pick here to a Bengals loss. Pick: Ravens 31, Bengals 28.

Our original predictions: Kelsey Conway had a Ravens win, Jason Williams and I had Bengals wins.

Week 8: Bengals vs. Tennessee Titans, 1 p.m., Nov. 1, CBS

Updated outlook: The 0-5 Titans are who we thought they were, and maybe even a little worse. The Bengals should survive this home game, but it will be unsatisfying like the win against the Dolphins. It could also look like the late-season win over Tennessee in 2024. I'm sticking with my original pick: Bengals 30, Titans 27.

Our original predictions: All three members of our Bengals coverage team had Cincinnati beating Tennessee.

Week 9: Bengals at Atlanta Falcons, 9:30 a.m., Nov. 8, NFL Network (Madrid)

Updated outlook: My original prediction was a 31-point Bengals win at the Santiago Bernabéu Stadium, home field of famous Spanish soccer club Real Madrid. I no longer think that's possible as Atlanta has shown flashes of tremendous upside under head coach Kevin Stefanski. The Falcons are built like a team that could eek out a win in this game. I'm flipping my pick to a Falcons win. Pick: Falcons 30, Bengals 24.

Our original predictions: All three members of our Bengals coverage team had Cincinnati beating Atlanta in Madrid.

Week 10: Bengals vs. Steelers, 8:20 p.m., Nov. 15, NBC Sunday Night Football

Updated outlook: I predicted a Bengals win in this game (of course, I also predicted the Bengals would win at Pittsburgh). But if Cincinnati enters with a 4-4 record, per my updated game predictions, this primetime game becomes an absolute must-win. At home, and considering the narrow-margin loss fraught with self-inflicted errors, giveaways and terrible tackling against bruising tight end Darnell Washington when these teams first met Sept. 27, I think the Bengals can do enough to eke out this win. So, I'll hang onto my original prediction of Bengals 20, Steelers 17.

Our original predictions: Kelsey Conway and Pat Brennan predicted Bengals wins while Jason Williams predicted a Steelers win.

Week 11: Bengals at Washington Commanders, 8:15 p.m., Nov. 23, ESPN Monday Night Football

Updated outlook: In Week 5, Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels returned from a two-week injury absence and posted this stat line: 17-of-25 passing for 199 yards (no interceptions); nine carries for 103 yards and two rushing touchdowns. We'll set aside the fact that Daniels was on the field in overtime as Washington ran out the clock in against the New York Giants, creating an all-time blunder of time mismanagement that produced a tie. If Daniels is healthy and plays like that against Cincinnati, a game I already thought the Bengals will lose could be very ugly. Keep in mind this game will conclude a stretch of three straight primetime games starting with the Falcons game in Madrid. The Bengals will be gassed, so I'm increasing my margin of defeat for this re-pick from 31-21 to Commanders 38, Bengals 17.

Our original predictions: All three members of our Bengals coverage team predicted the Commanders would win.

Week 12: Bengals vs. New Orleans Saints, 1 p.m., Nov. 29, CBS

Updated outlook: The Bengals aren't who I thought they'd be, but I feel the same way about the Saints (now 1-4 through five games). I'm decreasing the margin of victory but still giving the Bengals a convincing win. Pick: Bengals 31, Saints 17.

Our original predictions: All three members of our Bengals coverage team predicted a Cincinnati win.

Week 13: Bengals at Cleveland Browns, 1 p.m., Dec. 6, CBS

Updated outlook: I had given some thought to the Browns being a force in the AFC race for wild card berths, but then Cleveland dropped a 17-12 game to the New York Jets. I'll still give Cincinnati the edge over Cleveland. Pick: Bengals 28, Browns 17.

Our original predictions: Kelsey Conway and Pat Brennan predicted Bengals wins while Jason Williams predicted a Browns win.

Week 14: Bengals vs. Kansas City Chiefs, 4:25 p.m., Dec. 13, FOX

Updated outlook: Initially, I thought this game could live up to the classic Bengals-Chiefs encounters of yore, but only the Chiefs are holding up their end of the bargain so far at 4-0 through five weeks (Kansas City had its bye in Week 5). Based on what we've seen of the Bengals defense so far, 37-year-old Travis Kelce could still cut Cincinnati's defense into ribbons. You can say the same for KC running back Kenneth Walker III. We haven't seen the Bengals defense put a complete game together, and while improvement is possible by mid-December (perhaps likely), I no longer think Cincinnati can match and beat the aging, fading, dynastic Chiefs. Pick: Chiefs 31, Bengals 20.

Our original predictions: Kelsey Conway predicted a Chiefs win. Pat Brennan and Jason Williams predicted one-point Bengals wins.

Week 15: Bengals at Carolina Panthers , 1 p.m., Dec. 20, FOX

Updated outlook: The Panthers and Falcons look like they'll go head-to-head in the race for the NFC South in 2026. Since that looks like it could be a very tight race with the eventual division champ posting a modest record (Carolina is 2-2 entering Week 6), the game might just mean more to the Panthers. I have the Bengals at 7-5 entering this game, so it'll mean plenty to them, too, but I'm keeping my original pick of: Panthers 29, Bengals 24.

Our original predictions: Kelsey Conway and Jason Williams predicted Bengals wins while Pat Brennan predicted a Panthers win.

Week 16: Bengals at Indianapolis Colts, TBD, Dec. 26 or Dec. 27

Updated outlook: This game is still screaming out to me with these words: "The Lou Anarumo Revenge Game." I'm screaming out that I'm holding steady on my original prediction of: Colts 24, Bengals 16.

Our original predictions: All three members of our Bengals coverage team predicted Colts wins.

Week 17: Bengals vs. Baltimore Ravens, 8:15 p.m., Dec. 31, Amazon Prime Thursday Night Football

Updated outlook: So much for the idea that Cincinnati might catch the rest of the AFC North in a transition year as the three other organizations all settled into new head coaching regimes. After starting 4-1 with some formidable obstacles including an injury to Lamar Jackson, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter looks like the real deal. Maybe Baltimore is close to wrapping up the division by this point in the year. Maybe the Bengals need to have this game to stay alive in a push for a wild card spot, but I also have them at 7-8 at this point. That means their playoff hopes are likely hanging by a thread. This New Year's Eve game is a long way away, but unless the Bengals defense takes major steps forward, I don't see how they take a game off this Ravens team this year. My pick actually stays this same for this particular game, but the circumstances I foresee by Week 17 are drastically different from what I imagined prior to Week 1. Pick Ravens 31, Bengals 24.

Our original predictions: Pat Brennan and Jason Williams predicted Ravens wins while Kelsey Conway predicted a Bengals win.

Week 18: Bengals vs. Cleveland Browns, TBD, Jan. 9 or Jan. 10

Updated outlook: If my updated predictions hold up, Cincinnati is 7-9 entering this game, and basically staring into the abyss. It's a home game, but fans wouldn't be very engaged given the circumstances. Cincinnati can have this one, but only because the Browns will be more checked out than the hosts. Pick: Bengals 29, Browns 10.

Our original predictions: All three members of our Bengals coverage team predicted Bengals wins.

Updated Bengals 2026 predictions, and how I got there

My current expectations of the Bengals are a three-game swing from when I went to bed on Sept. 12, the eve of the season opener against the Buccaneers. That night, I thought the Bengals were an 11-6 team and an AFC North champion that would win a playoff game. I imagined the Bengals would host multiple playoff games (that would have been a first in the Zac Taylor era, by the way).

As of Week 6, I no longer expect any of those things. I anticipate Cincinnati will finish 8-9, miss the playoffs, and I see it that way because:

The defense isn't good enough. They still miss too many tackles and as good as Dexter Lawrence II, Boye Mafe, Jonathan Allen and the new faces brought in this past offseason have been, the weak spots at linebacker and safety are too much to compensate for.

The Bengals can't or won't run the ball. Six weeks into the season, there's an open question about whether Samaje Perine or Chase Brown should be the starting running back, and neither player looks capable of taking over a game. Perine was more effective against the Dolphins. Brown had the best single-game rushing output so far (80 yards vs. Houston). Joe Burrow carrying the ball is terrifying. Any way you look at what the Bengals do in this area of the game, they're underwhelming. And as much as people like to think there's always a heave-it-up-to-Ja'Marr-or-Tee option, you can't survive off that alone.

Burrow's protection has held up well enough, but the offensive line is thin. Hopefully, Dalton Risner is significantly more healthy after the bye week. Even while apparently compromised physically, he still stayed on the field against the Jacksonville Jaguars and wasn't as effective. The Dolphins game was better as Burrow wasn't sacked and was hit only a handful of times. Helping Orlando Brown Jr., who has struggled at times, takes something away from the offense, too. And even when Burrow's protection is decent, he's still capable of extending a play that results in more contact (Sept. 27 vs. the Steelers) or diving into places he shouldn't for fumbles (Oct. 11 vs. Dolphins). Burrow turns 30 in December. He is beloved for his style of play, but he's still putting himself in harm's way like this at this stage in his career? Against Miami, he emerged with only a jammed thumb on his non-throwing hand after diving for a fumbled ball, but anything could happen to Burrow's body when he chooses to play the game this way. That's a concern for this season, and beyond.

articles.title: Postgame: Avalanche Salvage a Point Against Stars Despite Shorthanded Mistake
articles.summary: Defeating the same team on consecutive nights is no easy feat, especially when you’re going head-to-head with another powerhouse Central […]
articles.body:
Defeating the same team on consecutive nights is no easy feat, especially when you're going head-to-head with another powerhouse Central Division rival.

The Colorado Avalanche couldn't quite secure a win against the Dallas Stars on Wednesday night at Ball Arena. They defeated them in Dallas the previous night but managed to collect a point at home. In the end, the Stars won 3-2 in a shootout.

Gabe Landeskog and Brock Nelson scored for the Avs. They also got a lone shootout tally from Nazem Kadri on four attempts. The Avs fell to 4-2-1 on the season and 2-1-1 against the Central Division.

They collected three of four points in two nights and surrendered two to the Stars.

"Every time we play these guys, it's a close game," head coach Jared Bednar said. "It's a hard-fought game, and yeah, ends up in a shootout, and we just came up a little bit short. But overall effort from our guys two nights in a row was pretty solid."

Dallas had goals from Miro Heiskanen at even strength and Arttu Hyry shorthanded. The Stars went 2-for-4 in the shootout, with both Jason Robertson and Roope Hintz beating goalie Scott Wedgewood.

It was the third shorthanded goal the Avalanche have surrendered in seven games, tying them with the Vancouver Canucks for the most in the NHL.

"We want to try and nip some things in the bud and make sure we're improving on a daily basis in every area of our game, including power play," Bednar said.

The Avalanche had two goals called back before the first period was halfway through. Less than two minutes in, the third line combined for a spectacular tic-tac-toe play that went from T.J. Hughes to Fedor Svechkov to Jaden Schwartz, who went to the backhand and put it past goalie Casey DeSmith. The Stars challenged the entry for offside, and the challenge was successful. Hughes was across the line before Schwartz carried the puck in.

The Avs didn't let it bother them. They kept attacking after killing off a penalty and eventually drew one of their own. With Jamie Benn in the box, Colorado didn't do much with its two minutes on the man advantage. But just as Benn re-entered the game, a Schwartz one-timer from the right circle bounced off Landeskog and trickled in.

There was no coach's challenge on that one, but there was a league-imposed review to determine whether Landeskog had kicked the puck in. This review lasted much longer than the first one and eventually ended with another goal wiped off the board.

"If you watch it in real speed, there's no chance I can react to that and kick that, but the guys in Toronto make the call," Landeskog said. "Not the first time they take one away, and probably not the last one. It's okay."

The first period ended scoreless, with the two clubs combining for 9:44 of power-play time.

In the second, the Avs eventually drew first blood. It was another play that bounced in off Landeskog, who scored his second goal of the season. But the play started with a great keep at the blue line by Sam Malinski. He was able to hold the puck in the zone when a Dallas player attempted a clear. He sent it to Kadri, who shot it in off Landeskog to make it 1-0 at 4:55.

Colorado carried that lead for well over 10 minutes, but the Stars responded at 15:03. Mikko Rantanen fended off Landeskog before sending a slick cross-ice pass to Heiskanen. Dallas' top blueliner fired it past Wedgewood for his third goal of the season.

Just as the third period began, Rantanen was called for tripping. The Avs, who were 0-for-3 on the power play, had another chance to break through. They not only failed to set up or create any dangerous looks but also gave up a shorthanded breakaway goal to Arttu Hyry. Again, it happened with the top unit on the ice.

The Avalanche failed to do anything with the remainder of the power play. Moments later, Gavin Brindley, making his season debut, fired a shot that hit the crossbar behind DeSmith and came back out. Brindley thought he had scored for a moment before continuing his shift. On the very next play, Kadri hit one off the post and was in disbelief when the puck bounced out the other side. The Avs seemingly had no puck luck.

At 8:21, Nelson found the back of the net after the puck hit Thomas Harley in front and landed on his stick with an open net to shoot at. The play started on Makar's stick at the point. He found Kadri, who set up Lehkonen for the one-timer that Harley blocked. At that point, it was tied 2-2, with the shots on goal even at 20-20. It was anybody's game.

Lehkonen and Fedor Svechkov each had a good look before the end of regulation but were stopped by DeSmith. The Stars netminder made 25 saves, while Wedgewood stopped 20.

As I said earlier, it felt like the Avalanche didn't have any puck luck. The goals that were called back, the shots off the crossbar and post. Nothing was really going their way.

Until it did with the Nelson goal. They worked for that one and secured a point they probably wouldn't have gotten had it not been for that sequence.

I really am a firm believer that defeating the same team on consecutive nights is a tough task. To be able to get that third point is big. It still would've been nice to see them close it out. Or not let in a second goal that was as self inflicted as they come.

There isn't much to be said about this that hasn't already been said.

The Avalanche can't figure out the power play, and it feels like they, again, need to try something entirely different. I'm starting to question whether Makar makes sense on the top unit and whether he needs more coaching to be the guy up there. The power play should run through him, but it feels like his confidence in shooting the puck has faded more and more with each passing year.

We've all seen the rumors and reports about Dave Hakstol's departure and his replacement being Brett McLean. This sounds like it's going to happen as early as Thursday. I don't know much about McLean's background or how he runs power plays, but a new voice couldn't be worse than what they have now. We'll see if he can crack the code.

articles.title: Atlanta man arrested in shooting of 49ers player as 3 others face charges
articles.summary: An Atlanta man is one of four people arrested in connection with a February shooting that injured a San Francisco 49ers player at a nightclub, according to p...
articles.body:
An Atlanta man is one of four people arrested in connection with a February shooting that injured a San Francisco 49ers player, Keion White, at a nightclub, according to police.

Marquis Davis, 38, was arrested Oct. 7 by Atlanta police on a warrant from the San Francisco Police Department. Investigators also seized an illegal firearm and several types of drugs during searches connected to the investigation.

The arrests were part of San Francisco police's Operation D-Line, a months-long investigation involving more than 50 search warrants and assistance from more than 250 law enforcement personnel nationwide.

The shooting happened Feb. 9 inside a nightclub on the 1700 block of Mission Street in San Francisco. Officers found the victim with a gunshot wound to the ankle. The player was taken to a hospital with injuries that were not considered life-threatening.

During the arrest of Davis, investigators recovered 820 grams of MDMA, 1,026 grams of methamphetamine, 979 grams of cocaine and 3,842 grams of fentanyl, along with an illegal firearm. Atlanta police separately reported recovering 59 pounds of marijuana during searches associated with Davis.

Three other suspects were arrested as part of the investigation.

Antoine Washington, 36, was arrested Oct. 7 in Stockton, California. Officers recovered a loaded firearm, more than 120 oxycodone pills and approximately $6,691 in cash, according to San Francisco police.

Curtis Green, 35, was taken into custody Oct. 7 at his home in Irvine, California. Gregory Walker, 36, was arrested Oct. 9 in Southern California.

Green and Walker were booked into San Francisco County Jail on Oct. 12 on charges including assault with a firearm. San Francisco police and prosecutors are working with other jurisdictions to arrange for Davis and Washington to be brought to San Francisco.

Davis was also charged in Georgia with multiple counts of trafficking controlled substances, multiple gang-related offenses and possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony. He was taken to the Fulton County Jail.

The investigation into the shooting is ongoing.

Anyone with information is asked to contact the San Francisco Police Department at 415-575-4444 or text a tip to TIP411 beginning the message with SFPD. Tips may be submitted anonymously.

articles.title: Martín Satriano desmonta el tópico contra el Getafe de Bordalás: "No ven nuestros partidos"
articles.standfirst: El delantero uruguayo defendió en 'La Tribu' que muchos juzgan al equipo de Bordalás sin ver sus partidos y recordó que “todos los equipos son intensos” y usan sus armas para ganar
articles.summary: El delantero uruguayo defendió en 'La Tribu' que muchos juzgan al equipo de Bordalás sin ver sus partidos y recordó que “todos los equipos son intensos” y usan sus armas para ganar
articles.body: Martín Satriano no esquivó el debate que lleva años persiguiendo al Getafe. El delantero uruguayo atendió a La Tribu en la previa del estreno azulón en la Conference League ante el Universitatea Craiova y defendió con claridad la forma de competir del equipo de Bordalás. El de Montevideo llega a la cita europea después de regresar de la convocatoria con Uruguay, ya recuperado de las molestias en la rodilla y con el foco puesto en el Getafe. “Ya he recuperado el 100% para el partido de Conference”, confirmó Satriano, que también reconoció que en verano hubo opciones para salir, aunque siempre tuvo clara su prioridad: “En mí siempre estuvo la idea de quedarme”. Satriano no cree que el Getafe sea el único equipo que utiliza la intensidad como herramienta. Al contrario, considera que el fútbol actual camina en esa dirección en todos los niveles. “Hoy en día todos los equipos son intensos, todos los equipos son agresivos”, explicó el delantero. El uruguayo puso incluso un ejemplo fuera de LaLiga para reforzar su argumento. “Yo he visto al Arsenal hacer tiempo para ganar un partido también. Y es fútbol, no tiene nada de malo, no entiendo por qué se ve mal eso”, señaló. Para Satriano, competir, manejar los tiempos y usar los recursos disponibles forma parte del juego. Su conclusión fue sencilla: “Uno usa las armas que tiene para ganar”. En el Getafe, esa idea no se vive como una excusa ni como una etiqueta incómoda, sino como parte de una identidad competitiva que les ha llevado de nuevo a Europa. El regreso continental del Getafe llega seis años después. El equipo de Bordalás debuta en la Conference League ante el Craiova en Rumanía, una cita que Satriano afronta ya recuperado de las molestias en la rodilla. “Muy bien, la verdad, ya he recuperado el 100% para el partido de Conference”, confirmó. Para el delantero, jugar esta competición con el Getafe tiene un valor especial. “Para un equipo como el Getafe hoy en día jugar Conference League es algo único, algo que tenemos que disfrutar mucho”, afirmó. Eso sí, el plan no cambia: ir partido a partido, competir y tratar de avanzar lo máximo posible. El calendario, además, exigirá al máximo a una plantilla que afronta Liga, Copa y Conference. Satriano admitió que jugar tres competiciones “no es fácil”, pero no quiso instalar ninguna queja. “No hay nada más lindo que competir, que jugar al fútbol”, aseguró, antes de recordar que “la Liga no la podés cuidar, porque es lo que te da de comer”. Satriano también habló de su situación personal y del contexto que ha encontrado en el Getafe. Después de varios años cambiando de equipo, el uruguayo encontró estabilidad en el Coliseum. “En mí siempre estuvo la idea de quedarme”, reconoció al ser preguntado por posibles ofertas para salir durante el verano. El delantero explicó que llegó al Getafe buscando continuidad y encontró un entorno en el que se siente cómodo. En ese camino, Bordalás ha tenido un papel clave: “Mucha confianza me da el míster, los compañeros, el club. Me siento muy cómodo acá. Es como una familia, Getafe”, afirmó. Esa confianza le permite adaptarse a distintas posiciones. Aunque su zona natural está arriba, Satriano no tiene problema en caer a banda si el equipo lo necesita. “Yo siempre me siento cómodo jugando, da igual donde sea. Donde lo pide el míster, ahí voy a estar”, explicó. El uruguayo también valoró la llegada de Carvajal al vestuario. “Es un fenómeno”, dijo sobre el lateral, al que ve humilde y con hambre pese a todo lo que ha ganado. “Te transmite que todavía tiene muchas ganas y eso está bueno”, añadió. En ataque, Satriano destacó además su buena conexión con Ünal desde el primer día y evitó ponerse una cifra concreta de goles. El objetivo, dijo, pasa por superarse, seguir creciendo y ayudar al equipo. El Getafe inicia ahora su camino europeo con una idea clara: competir sin complejos y sin pedir perdón por su manera de jugar. Satriano lo resumió mejor que nadie: en el fútbol todos usan sus armas, y al final lo que queda es ganar partidos.

articles.title: Así es el extraño Porsche 911 Turbo que Ron Dennis se compró cuando era Dtor. de McLaren
articles.standfirst: Se trata de un 911 Turbo que el jefe de Mclaren adquirió en 1986. Pero venía tan cargado de extras que costaba el doble que un 911 Turbo de serie
articles.summary: Se trata de un 911 Turbo que el jefe de McLaren adquirió en 1986 y que venía tan cargado de extras, que costaba el doble que un 911 Turbo de serie
articles.body: Que un Porsche 911 Turbo salga a subasta este 14 de noviembre en el NEC Classic Motor Show de Birmingham no es noticia. Solo que en este caso no se trata de un 911 cualquiera, sino de una unidad SE ‘Flachbau’ (es decir, de morro plano) que encargó en 1986 Ron Dennis, que como bien saben los aficionados a la Fórmula 1 (y muy bien los españoles) fue durante muchos años el 'mandamás' en McLaren. En concreto, Dennis fue entre 1981 y 2009 director del equipo, director ejecutivo y copropietario de McLaren en Fórmula 1. Fue un tiempo en el que el equipo ganó siete títulos de constructores, entre 1984 y 1998, y diez de pilotos, con Niki Lauda (1984), Alain Prost (1985, 1986 y 1989), Ayrton Senna (1988, 1990 y 1991), Mika Häkkinen (1998 y 1999) y Lewis Hamilton (2008). ‘Flachbau’ significa en alemán ‘construcción baja’ y alude al morro plano de los 935 de competición, que acabó ofreciéndose en los 911 de calle como una opción costosísima que no todos los clientes estaban dispuestos a pagar. Esta versión SE era una opción totalmente a medida y hecha en gran medida a mano, con el motor Turbo S de 335 CV, y costaba más del doble que un 930 Turbo de serie cuando era nuevo. Ahora bien, su importancia no consiste solo en que su carrocería se parezca más a la de los modelos de competición. También es uno de los apenas 50 modelos de fábrica con volante a la derecha y, según Iconic Auctioneers, la casa que se va a encargar de subastarlo, es único por su historial y sus especificaciones y uno de los dos Flachbau más importantes. ¿Y el otro? Pertenecía a Mansour Ojjeh, empresario saudí y director ejecutivo del Grupo TAG, que encargó su 911 Turbo Coupé de 1983 con carrocería tipo 935 y 380 CV. Ojjeh y Dennis se conocieron en 1981, se hicieron amigos y socios, y Ojjeh acabó siendo el accionista mayoritario de McLaren, con el 60% de las participaciones. Además, invirtió en motores turbo fabricados por Porsche que llevaban el nombre de su empresa, TAG. Así que, siendo dos amigos, encargaron dos Porsche a medida. Nada extraño hay en ello. El 911 de Dennis lleva un equipo de audio especial de la firma Blaupunkt con altavoces traseros en una bandeja hecha a medida, un indicador LED de la presión del turbo (poco habitual) a la derecha del cuadro y un panel central de caoba con reloj, voltímetro e indicador de temperatura ambiente. Todo ello puesto a la carta por Porsche, no por un preparador posterior. La historia del coche está respaldada por documentos dirigidos a Ron Dennis como titular y la confirmación de Porsche que detalla las opciones a medida encargadas por el británico. Pero a su favor (es decir, al hecho de que sea más caro) también está su bajísimo kilometraje, que en la actualidad es de solo 4.200 km: poco más de 100 km al año de media. Ahora el coche ha pasado por una puesta a punto exhaustiva y su futuro propietario podrá presumir de contar con uno de los Porsche 911 Turbo más especiales que existen. Eso sí, para conseguirlo tendrá antes que ganar la puja el próximo 14 de noviembre, para lo que tendrá que pagar un precio que se estima entre 415.000 y 475.000 euros.

articles.title: 'Heartbroken' Washington state superintendent says no consequences for girls who protested transgender runner
articles.summary: Camas School District superintendent John Anzalone says girls who walked off the cross country starting line in protest will face no repercussions.
articles.body: For one question, Camas School District superintendent John Anzalone chose not to answer as an administrator, but rather a father. He has been navigating what may be the most contentious, controversial sports story in the country right now and understands the angst it has caused numerous teenagers. That angst came to a head Tuesday when about a dozen runners from the Camas High School girls cross country team walked off the starting line when the gun went off in their race against Battle Ground, a fellow Washington state school. Why? They were protesting their male teammate competing against the females. WASHINGTON GIRLS WALK OFF CROSS COUNTRY MEET IN PROTEST OF MALE ATHLETE, PARENTS REVEAL HOW IT CAME TO THIS Last month, a Camas sophomore switched to the girls team midseason after finishing 76th in a boys race. He has since won a varsity meet and placed second in two others. Unsurprisingly, this has ballooned into a national story with teammates and opponents staging protests. Anzalone didn't take a side on the issue, but he empathizes with the students' plight. "It's always hard to see when students are upset, let alone our families. And I know this issue has polarized our country for a long time, and this has probably added to that, right," Anzalone said. "And so, as a dad, it's always hard to see your own kids or any kids in the middle of something like this. And that's probably been the most heartbreaking for me, is to see certain students really kind of in the middle of this, right? They're kids. So that's been challenging, and that's always gonna be hard." It's hard to know exactly how Anzalone or anyone involved with the school feels about the biological male competing in these meets after starting the year with the boys. They have been either neutral (Anzalone) or mute (the coaching staff) when asked about the topic. But at a meet in Arlington, Washington, last Saturday, numerous parents made their disapproval clear. And increasingly, the athletes are doing the same. This isn't an easy thing to do. Despite most of the country supporting the separation of biological males and females in sports, the vocal minority can be vicious. A parent last week told me he didn't want to talk because "I don't want my house burned down," while one girl who protested last month said some of her friends stopped acknowledging her. DAD BANNED FROM SCHOOL GROUNDS AFTER PROTESTING TRANS RUNNER COMPETING AGAINST HIS DAUGHTER But Anzalone wanted to make clear that there will not be consequences for the Camas girls who walked off the line Tuesday. "The girls are entitled to handle this however is best for them, and I was at the meet and it was peacefully done. And of course, we'll support whatever they want to do," Anzalone said. "I felt that this wasn't just about supporting and protecting (the male runner). This was really about supporting and providing that space for the girls who did walk off to do so and not feel any repercussions. And of course, some of them looked very sad. I think some of them were very conflicted. But they're also teenagers. They're still children." Next on the Camas cross country schedule is the Greater St. Helen's League district meet on Oct. 21. A parent of one of the Camas runners who protested Tuesday said she isn't sure how the girls will proceed. But the district meet allows for only seven varsity runners from each team, meaning the male runner will very likely displace one of his female teammates. Anzalone said there will be no action taken to prevent such a scenario. WASHINGTON OFFICIALS WON'T BUDGE ON TRANS ATHLETE POLICY AFTER GIRL FILES SCOTUS APPEAL FOR ALLEGED ASSAULT "As long as WIAA policy allows (the biological male) to run, and she's eligible to run, she'll continue running. Nothing's changed," Anzalone said. "We don't make political stances as a school district. We just won't, and we can't. And so, as long as the policy stands, we're going to follow the policy." The male runner's midseason switch violated no rules. Under Washington Interscholastic Activities Association (WIAA) policy, students are permitted to compete on teams consistent with their gender identity. This could change soon, though. On the November 3 ballot in Washington is Initiative 638, which would require students in K-12 sports to compete on teams corresponding to their biological sex. A spokesperson for Let's Go Washington — the group behind the initiative — said the measure would take effect 30 days after the November 3 election (although delays in certifying the results could push back that timeline.) Cross country season would be over by then, but I-638 would prevent similar situations from arising in the future. Anzalone said Camas would comply with whatever rules are in place. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "I'm at a point where I have to stand by policy and by law," he said. "And like I said earlier, if those change or go in a different direction, we'll follow that." The Camas School District issued its own statement on the matter Wednesday. "Camas School District recognizes that students and community members hold differing views about athletic eligibility and have the right to express those views peacefully. Our responsibility is to ensure that school-sponsored events remain safe and respectful for all participants, staff, and spectators. As a Washington public school district and member of the Washington Interscholastic Activities Association (WIAA), Camas follows applicable state law and WIAA eligibility rules. RCW 28A.642 prohibits discrimination in public schools based on gender identity and gender expression, and current WIAA rules permit students to participate in athletics consistent with their gender identity. The district does not set these eligibility standards independently. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP We will continue to prioritize student safety, privacy, and well-being. We do not discuss individual students' eligibility, personal circumstances, or potential disciplinary matters."

articles.title: 10 Most Expensive Sports Card and Memorabilia Sales of 2026
articles.summary: The high-end sports card and memorabilia market has reached new heights in 2026, with multiple sales crossing the $10 million threshold as significant pieces of sports history and ultra-rare cards have made national news after changing hands.
articles.body:
The high-end sports card and memorabilia market has reached new heights in 2026, with multiple sales crossing the $10 million threshold as significant pieces of sports history and ultra-rare cards have made national news after changing hands.

There is still time for the final leaderboard to have some new entries, but for now, we've put together a rundown of the 10 most expensive sports card and memorabilia sales of 2026, starting with a sale that was just announced earlier this month.

The list features two basketball jerseys, one soccer shirt and seven sports cards, and they all sold for $4,880,000 or more.

Pro athletes we'd want to see play other sports

10 MOST EXPENSIVE SPORTS CARD/MEMORABILIA SALES OF 2026

Sale Price: $14,000,000 | Date: Sept. 2026

The Game 1 jersey from the 1998 NBA Finals sold for $10.1 million in 2022, setting a new record for a Michael Jordan memorabilia item. That record was seemingly overtaken by the Game 3 jersey from the same series in mid-September of this year, until Hunt Auctions announced in early October that this sale had actually closed before the Game 3 transaction in September.

What price will we see if the Game 6 "Last Shot" jersey ever hits the auction block?

Sale Price: $12,260,000 | Date: Sept. 2026

This 1998 NBA Finals Game 3 jersey, sold by Pharrell Williams' JOOPITER auction house, has the unique distinction of being worn in what turned out to be the most lopsided game in NBA Finals history. The Bulls won 96-54 behind a game-high 24 points from Jordan, taking a 2-1 series lead after their Game 1 loss.

Sale Price: $11,000,000 | Date: July 2026 | Grade: Ungraded

The Gold Logoman program was introduced for the 2025 season, highlighting the winners of the MVP, Cy Young and Rookie of the Year from the previous season with a gold logoman patch on their uniforms. In 2026, Topps released a trio of Back to Back Gold Logoman cards for Shohei Ohtani, Aaron Judge and Tarik Skubal, as they had won hardware in back-to-back years.

The Ohtani card not only features gold logoman patches from his 2024 and 2025 MVP seasons, but also dual autographs, one in English and one in Kanji. It was sold ungraded immediately after being pulled from a pack, and now carries a PSA 9/Auto 10 grade.

Sale Price: $8,040,000 | Date: Sept. 2026 | Grade: PSA 10/Auto 10

Viewed as a potential generational talent, Cooper Flagg averaged 21.0 points, 6.7 rebounds and 4.5 assists in his debut to win Rookie of the Year honors, and he may be just scratching the surface of his potential. That upside is clearly reflected in the purchase price of what is unquestionably his most sought-after rookie card, featuring a 1-of-1 patch worn in his NBA debut along with an autograph.

Sale Price: $6,501,840 | Date: Sept. 2026 | Grade: PSA 8/Auto 10

This card is part of the same legendary set that features a Michael Jordan and Kobe Bryant dual logoman auto that sold for $12,932,000 in 2025, the highest price ever paid for a sports card. While many premium cards like this are immediately sold by the person who pulls them, this one sat in a private collection, ungraded for almost 20 years.

Sale Price: $5,856,000 | Date: Aug. 2026 | Grade: SGC Authentic

The Honus Wagner T206 card is arguably the most iconic sports card of all time. It was the first card ever to sell for more than $1 million back in 2000, and the highest recorded sale of a copy was an SGC 2 that sold for $7.25 million in 2022. This is one of only three known examples with the "Piedmont" back, with most copies carrying "Sweet Caporal" advertising.

Sale Price: $5,200,000 | Date: March 2026 | Grade: BGS 9.5/Auto 10

One of the best players to debut since "1st Bowman" cards became a focal point of the hobby doesn't actually have a card with that distinction. The 2013 Bowman Chrome Draft set contains what is widely recognized as Aaron Judge's first Bowman autograph, even without the familiar "1st Bowman" logo. That explains why this superfractor fetched such a high price, as it stands as his top pre-rookie card.

Sale Price: $5,124,000 | Date: Feb. 2026 | Grade: PSA 1

That's right, two separate Honus Wagner T206 cards sold for more than $5 million in 2026, and a third just missed cracking the top 10 with a $3,599,000 sale price back in March. Production of Wagner's T206 card was halted early, and an estimated 50 to 200 copies remain in existence, making it the holy grail of vintage cards.

Sale Price: $5,110,000 | Date: May 2026 | Grade: PSA 10

In an interesting licensing conflict, Panini held the exclusive NBA trading card license during Victor Wembanyama's 2023-24 rookie season, while he personally had an exclusive autograph deal with Fanatics. As a result, none of his official NBA cards feature autographs, putting this 1-of-1 black parallel at the very top of his rookie-card market.

Sale Price: $4,880,000 | Date: July 2026

Pelé scored six goals in four matches during the 1958 World Cup, despite the fact that he was only 17 years old. He still stands as the youngest player ever to appear in a World Cup final, and he ended up scoring two goals in Brazil's victory over Sweden. It was a lucrative year for high-profile soccer memorabilia, as the game-used ball from Maradona's iconic "Hand of God" goal also sold for $3,355,000 in August.

With no end in sight to the surging high-end sports memorabilia market, expect plenty more headline-grabbing sales in 2027.

For now, these 10 stand out as the biggest sales of 2026, and there's still time for something to steal a spot before the year comes to a close.

articles.title: Llega el primer España contra Euskadi en un Mundial absoluto
articles.standfirst: El campeonato del Mundo que arranca en Buenos Aires se inagura con un partido de paleta goma entre el equipo femenino español y el vasco
articles.summary: El campeonato del Mundo que arranca en Buenos Aires se inagura con un partido de pelota goma entre el equipo femenino español y el vasco
articles.body: El primer España-Euskadi en un Mundial absoluto de pelota ya es una realidad. Desde que la Federación Internacional reconoció a la Federación Vasca como miembro de pleno de derecho, en diciembre de 2024, se había dado ya varios duelos entre ambas selecciones, pero no en un campeonato del Mundo absoluto. Buenos Aires acoge esta cita hasta el 24 de octubre con nueve disciplinas: frontball', frontenis, mano individual y parejas, cesta punta, pala corta, paleta cuero, paleta goma, pelota adaptada y xare. El partido inaugural dejará ya el primer España-Euskadi de la historia. Será el duelo entre los equipos femeninos de paleta goma que abrirá la navarra Maider Ardanaz, por España, frente a la alavesa Nagore Martin, por Euskadi. El equipo español acude con 58 pelotaris, entre los que hay ocho vascos (en cesta femenina y masculina y trinquete mano y xare) y 32 navarros, el resto son de La Rioja, Canarias, Castilla y León y Cataluña. Además, el equipo técnico lo forman siete navarros, dos valencianos y un vasco. Estará presente en todas las modalidades salvo pelota adaptada. Euskadi acude con 41 deportistas. "Hay un componente político que se lo dejo a los políticos, que para eso lo usan cuando quieren, y hay un componente deportivo que es el mío, que es el que me toca y ahí nada que decir: nosotros vamos a competir y listo. Nuestros deportistas llevan la bandera de España a un campeonato del mundo y realizan un esfuerzo extraordinario para competir al máximo nivel″, sostiene Javier Conde, presidente de la Federación Española en declaraciones a EFE. En el anterior Mundial, disputado en octubre de 2022 en Biarritz (Francia), España lideró el medallero con 20 metales (nueve oros, nueve platas y dos bronces), Francia fue segunda con 16, cinco de ellos de oro-, y México acabó tercero con diez preseas. Ahora, el equipo francés parte como favorito para ser el más laureado con la división de pelotaris entre España y Euskadi. Desde la entrada de la Federación Vasca en la Internacional en diciembre de 2024, el primer enfrentamiento entre España y Euskadi se vio en la Liga de Naciones de Gernika en junio de 2025. La Federación Española no reconoció la oficialidad de esta competición de cesta punta, organizada por la Federación Internacional y la Vasca. Los siguientes cara a cara llegaron en el Mundial sub 23 de trinquete en septiembre y el de la Liga de Naciones de Frontón 30 metros, disputada en Aguascalientes en octubre. Luego llegó, en noviembre de 2025, el enfrentamiento en la tercera edición del Mundial de frontball, modalidad que aspira a ser olímpica en Brisbane 2032, y unas semanas más tarde la I Liga de Naciones de 36 metros. El punto de partida de esta situación fue la entrada en vigor de la nueva Ley del Deporte el 1 de enero de 2023. El artículo 48.2, con un evidente trasfondo político que pretendía contentar al PNV, reconoce la posibilidad de que las federaciones deportivas autonómicas puedan participar directamente en el ámbito internacional "en el caso de modalidades o especialidades deportivas con arraigo histórico y social". La maquinaria echó a andar y desembocó en la Asamblea de la Internacional del 28 de diciembre de 2024 en Navarra y la votación favorable a la entrada de Euskadi. La Federación Española de Pelota presentó un recurso ante el Tribunal de Arbitraje Deportivo con el que impugnaba la votación. Ocurrió el 13 de enero cuando Julián García Angulo, presidente de la FEPelota desde 1991, encabezaba la comisión gestora durante el proceso electoral que acabaría con Javier Conde como nuevo presidente. Tras la presentación del recurso al TAS, la Federación Internacional de Pelota Vasca amenazó con expulsar a la española, mientras desde el Consejo Superior de Deportes se apelaba al diálogo y la búsqueda de un acuerdo entre todas las partes, incluido el Gobierno Vasco. Finalmente, la FIPV renunció a suspender o expulsar a España. Entremedias, declaraciones poco afortunadas como las Rodríguez Uribes, presidente del CSD, en las que llegó a decir que "la pelota vasca no es un deporte español en el sentido de que se practique en toda España". Mientras el tiempo pasaba a la espera de la decisión del TAS, el conflicto desembocó en los citados duelos entre España y Euskadi en varias competiciones. Antes la FIPV aprobó los requisitos que debían cumplir los pelotaris para competir con Euskadi: pasaporte Español, empadronamiento o residencia fiscal en las provincias de Guipúzcoa, Vizcaya o Álava y residencia mínima en cualquiera de las tres provincias de 36 meses cumplidos. Finalmente, en enero de 2026, el TAS se inhibió en la apelación presentada por la Federación Española de Pelota. Declinó la jurisdicción para revisar y resolver esta apelación. "Los estatutos de la FIVP no contienen una cláusula arbitral que permita impugnar ante el TAS las decisiones acordadas por su asamblea general", recogió el comunicado del TAS. Como consecuencia de todo este proceso, la Junta Directiva Federación Internacional de Pelota Vasca decidió trasladar su sede social desde Pamplona, donde había permanecido los últimos 24 años, hasta Biarritz (Francia). Ahora, se vive un nuevo capítulo deportivo con el primer Mundial absoluto de pelota en el que España y Euskadi se enfrentan como rivales.

articles.body:
The initial SEC Student-Athlete Availability Report has been released ahead of the Auburn Tigers ' road trip to No. 1 Georgia on Saturday.

The Tigers emerge from the bye week relatively healthy, with only two players, tight end Hunter Herring and offensive lineman Tai Buster, ruled out for Saturday's game at Georgia due to injury. However, the biggest news from the initial report is that linebacker Xavier Atkins is officially ruled out.

Atkins, who is tied for the team lead in sacks and second on the team in tackles, has been suspended for Saturday's game at No. 1 Georgia, according to Auburn head coach Alex Golesh. Golesh first mentioned the suspension during Monday's press conference and clarified Wednesday that Atkins is not with the team during practice this week. Golesh will address Atkins' status again next week.

The Bulldogs will be without several players, including running back Chauncey Bowens, who leads the team in rushing touchdowns with six. However, Georgia received potentially good news on Wednesday as running back Nate Frazier is not on the availability report after missing four straight games with a rib injury. He was not included on the availability report for Georgia's Week 6 game at Alabama ; however, he did not play.

articles.title: Penn State vs. Michigan: Game Preview
articles.summary: Can Penn State finally get back in the win column?
articles.body:
The Nittany Lions visit the Big House as they attempt to win their first Big Ten game of the season.

Penn State (3-3, 0-3) vs. Michigan (3-2, 0-2)

Kickoff: 3:30 p.m., Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor, MI

The Betting Line: Penn State +6.5 (Fanduel)

TV: CBS, 3:30 p.m., Brad Nessler (play-by-play), Charles Davis (analyst), Jenny Dell (sideline)

Weather: Sunny and dry, but a cool day with a high of 52 and temps dropping into the 30s in the evening.

Penn State set an all-time Beaver Stadium record during the White Out against USC, with 114,419 in attendance…Audavion Collins is second in the nation in pass breakups with eight…Michigan leads the all-time series 17-10 over Penn State…the Nittany Lions are second in the Big Ten in pass defense and third in turnover margin.

Penn State's offense has been bad. Michigan's has been atrocious. The Wolverines rank last or second-to-last in the Big Ten in scoring offense, total offense, passing offense, and explosive plays. They are 13th in rushing offense.

The biggest reason for Michigan's offensive woes is the lack of development for quarterback Bryce Underwood, the top prospect of the 2025 recruiting class. Underwood is in his second year as a starter, but hardly looks it. He routinely misses open receivers, and when he does spot them, he's had accuracy issues. He just has not looked like a functional Big Ten quarterback with a grasp of the position to succeed. Underwood is completing just 59 percent of his passes with five touchdowns to four interceptions. While he was able to find some rhythm against Iowa, he followed that up with his worst game of the season against Minnesota, completing 10-of-21 passes without a touchdown while being picked off twice.

For what Underwood lacks as a passer, he is a dangerous threat as a runner. The Wolverines have relied heavily on designed quarterback runs to get something out of the offense, and Saturday will be no exception. Opposing offenses have figured out how to get the Nittany Lion defense out of position for big gains on the ground. Michigan will surely have a heavy focus on the run throughout the afternoon.

Michigan's offensive line is not near the standard of the units that would maul defenses in the late Harbaugh era. They are an average line that has not been able to open holes for easy gains, and have allowed eight sacks on the season.

Running backs Jordan Marshall and Savion Hiter have been the workhorse backs for the offense. Marshall is a physical runner who does not shy away from contact. Hiter is a freshman still getting his feet wet, and averaged 0.8 yards per rush against Oklahoma and 1.1 yards in the loss to Minnesota.

JJ Buchanan and Andrew Marsh are the two leading receivers, and only players on the team with more than five catches this season. Buchanan is used to stretch the field as an explosive play threat, while Marsh is looked to often to keep the chains moving.

This match-up will tell us a lot about the Penn State defense. Michigan's offense has had trouble moving the ball, while Penn State's defense has struggled to make consistent stops in Big Ten play. The defensive line has been especially bad, generating no pass rush while being pushed around for easy running lanes. The linebacker play has been poor outside of Tony Rojas, and a big reason why teams have run so freely in recent weeks.

Rocco Becht has his best game in conference play against USC. Unfortunately, it wasn't enough to keep up with Jordan Maiva and the Trojans offense. This trend will need to continue after poor performances against Wisconsin and Northwestern. Unfortunately, the Nittany Lions do not have a reliable run game regardless of who is in the backfield, so Becht will need to bounce back play like the nation's most experienced quarterbacks if the season is going to be salvaged.

It's clear Becht misses Koby Howard, who was by far the most explosive option on the offense. Chase Sowell has looked good when given the opportunity, but was shut out in the second half after coming off the field briefly with an injury. Zay Robinson has proven he has playmaking ability as a return man, and could get more involved in the offense with eight catches for 122 yards and a score through six games.

Michigan's defense will be the clear best unit on the field on Saturday. They lead the Big Ten in total defense and passing defense, with the fourth best run defense giving up just 94 yards a game on the ground. The Nittany Lions will have their hands full moving the ball against this defense.

Troy Bowles, a former Georgia Bulldog, is on track to be an All-Big Ten linebacker. He has excellent quickness and instincts that make him a great sideline-to-sideline player while also making plays in the backfield. John Henry Daley and Nichols are a dynamic duo at defensive end, and will be a trouble spot for an offensive line that has struggled at the tackle position (and center and guard for that matter…). Cornerback Jyaire Hill is another standout who excels in coverage but also has the physicality to be a major run supporter and used in unexpected blitz packages.

Michigan kicker Trey Butkowski only has four field goal attempts, but has made all of them including a season-long 49 yarder. Punter Cam Brown is as steady as they come, averaging 43.3 yards per punt while placing nearly half of his attempts inside the 20.

Both teams have offenses that make fans want to pull out their hair in sheer frustration. I don't have confidence that either side can regularly move the ball, so expect a low scoring affair. The difference here is the Michigan defense. They will be the best unit on the field by quite a wide margin. They are much more reliable than Penn State's defense, which has only seemed to get worse from week to week.

Underwood makes some splash plays on the ground that lead to a touchdown and sets the Wolverines in scoring position enough to pull off the victory, handing Penn State its fourth consecutive loss.

articles.title: World Gymnastics regrets 'confusion' after 3 top Russians refused visas for world championships
articles.summary: ROTTERDAM, Netherlands (AP) — World Gymnastics says it regrets “confusion” ahead of the world championships starting on Saturday after three top Russians wer...
articles.body:
ROTTERDAM, Netherlands (AP) — World Gymnastics says it regrets "confusion" ahead of the world championships starting on Saturday after three top Russians were denied visas to enter the Netherlands for the event.

Former Olympic champions Angelina Melnikova and Viktoria Listunova, along with teammate Anna Kalmykova, were not allowed to travel to Rotterdam for the week-long worlds that are a team qualifying event for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics , the Russian team has said.

Other members of the Russian team have been given visas.

"The issuance of visas to all participants is a process determined solely by the Dutch authorities," World Gymnastics said Wednesday. "World Gymnastics is not in a position to explain why a select number of application requests have been refused.

"World Gymnastics remains in ongoing dialogue with the Dutch authorities, the Local Organizing Committee, and the Russian Gymnastics Federation. World Gymnastics fully regrets the negative impact on the preparations of the Russian delegation and the confusion felt among the wider Artistic Gymnastics World Championships community."

The cases illustrate how efforts in the sports world to lift many restrictions on Russian athletes and teams don't always mean host governments allow them to travel for events.

It also comes a year after the world championships went ahead in Indonesia without the Israeli team after authorities in the host country refused to issue visas.

Melnikova won the European all-around title in August in Croatia after being issued a visa following an initial refusal, the Russian team said at the time. Listunova was refused on that occasion.

Russia planned to demand the world championships be stripped of their Olympic qualifier status over the issue, sports minister Mikhail Degtyaryov wrote on social media on Tuesday.

World Gymnastics did not mention that demand in its statement and did not respond to a question about it from The Associated Press. The International Olympic Committee also did not address that demand in a statement Wednesday and said it could not comment on the individual cases.

"Ahead of the upcoming Artistic Gymnastics World Championships in Rotterdam, the IOC supported World Gymnastics in its efforts to ensure that all athletes could participate in this event," the IOC said.

"The vast majority of these athletes received their visas, and we have been informed by the International Federation that athletes will have other opportunities to qualify for the Olympic Games over the course of the next two years."

Russian gymnasts were cleared in May of restrictions to competing internationally by World Gymnastics, after years of being banned or required to pass vetting for neutral status during the full military invasion of Ukraine.

articles.title: Ravens’ Tyler Huntley Draws ‘Overused’ Praise From Browns’ Todd Monken
articles.summary: Before becoming head coach of the Cleveland Browns, Todd Monken was on the Baltimore Ravens coaching staff. He served as Baltimore’s offensive coordinator fr...
articles.body:
Before becoming head coach of the Cleveland Browns, Todd Monken was on the Baltimore Ravens coaching staff . He served as Baltimore's offensive coordinator from 2023 to 2025, where he worked with ultra-talented quarterback Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley.

Monken is now planning how to beat his former team, with the Browns and the Ravens set to meet this Sunday in Cleveland.

Monken Praises Huntley Ahead of Week 6 Browns-Ravens Clash

With Jackson in danger of missing another game due to an injury, Huntley looks poised to get another start under center for Baltimore, which is coming off a thrilling 30-23 overtime win over the Atlanta Falcons on the road in Week 5.

Monken gave Huntley his flowers ahead of the game.

"Very confident player. He has a belief in himself to make plays, and he's really a gamer," Monken said of Huntley when asked about why the quarterback has been a great fit alongside Jackson (h/t Irie Harris of Cleveland.com) .

"I know it sounds really overused, but the moment never gets too big for him. He loves to play football, and he gets in the game and he's able to make plays with his arms and his legs, and he gets rid of the ball and knows where to get the ball out when under duress," added Monken, who clearly watched Huntley help Baltimore win against the Falcons.

"And he works awfully hard. He's very diligent in preparing as the backup. So, when his time is called, he's able to play at a high level."

Huntley led the Ravens to two touchdown-scoring drives late in the fourth quarter and in overtime. He finished with 201 passing yards and two touchdowns on 24/32 pass completions. He added 20 rushing yards and a touchdown on six carries for Baltimore, which improved to 4-1.

articles.title: ’Ballhalla better be’ – Natalie Nakase sends ‘hostility’ message to Valkyries fans before WNBA Finals
articles.summary: The Golden State Valkyries’ home support is the stuff of legends, and head coach Natalie Nakase has outlined her expectations from them during the WNBA Final...
articles.body:
The Golden State Valkyries' home support is the stuff of legends, and head coach Natalie Nakase has outlined her expectations from them during the WNBA Finals.

In just their second season as a franchise, the Golden State Valkyries are already challenging for their first ever WNBA title. Led by Gabby Williams, the team has shown they are a very talented and exceptionally well-coached group. The Valks have another ace up their sleeve, too.

Golden State plays their home game at the Chase Center, and their popularity in San Francisco is through the roof. The team is incredibly popular, their fans have helped them become the first women's team to reach the $100 million in revenue mark. They are also very passionate and loud fans, so with the biggest series in franchise history coming up, the head coach is ready to see them show out.

Natalie Nakase says 'Ballhalla' has to be preparing a great gameplan for the WNBA Finals

For the uninitiated, 'Ballhalla' is what the Chase Center is referred to as during Valkyries home games. An obvious homage to Norse mythology's afterlife, it fits with the team name quite well. It's also an apt description for the high-intensity environment that those fans are capable of creating.

The Valkyries faithful don't need any extra motivation to bring their 'A-game' for the Finals, but Natalie Nakase has let them know of what is expected nonetheless.

"You guys know, since we're prepping for a great gameplan, Ballhalla better be prepping a gameplan," the head coach said. "As soon as they're announced, I need some hostility. As soon as, if they do challenge, I need some hostility. If they shoot free throws, I need that game to be rocking.

"So, gameplan, Ballhalla. Get ready, get prepped. Because we definitely need to use Ballhalla as our sixth man."

It is evident how much faith the coach has in the fans and their ability to influence the game. If the team is able to get the arena involved, the Dream will have an exceptionally hard time handling the Valkyries. The atmosphere alone is going to make the first two games of the WNBA Finals absolutely electric.

articles.title: Defensively sound Exeter need more goals - Taylor
articles.summary: Exeter City boss Matt Taylor says his side still has to improve their attacking output, despite their defensive strength.
articles.body:
Exeter City boss Matt Taylor says his side still has to improve their attacking output, despite their defensive strength.

The Grecians have conceded just six goals in their opening 10 games in League Two - the joint-best record in the division with Walsall.

It is also Exeter's second-best defensive record after 10 games in their history - one off the 1973-74 season and the 1986-87 campaign.

But the Grecians, who have won their past two games 1-0, have scored just six times in those 10 games - the third-worst record in the division.

"We're pleased with that 10-game split defensively, but we've still got to add so much more at the other end of the pitch," Taylor told BBC Radio Devon.

"We can't just say we've had a great 10 games in terms of our defensive output, and it's not just the defenders, it's not just the goalkeeper, it is every single one.

"Josh Gordon is our best defender because he's our first defender, then there was [George] Birch at the weekend and Anthony Scully and Taylor Perry, they are our best defenders because they're the first defenders.

"They protect the back line so much in terms of the way they play. So I'm delighted we've conceded six in 10, I still want the next 10 games to look like that in terms of a low return for opposition goals against us.

"But also we've got to find a way of scoring more than six goals ourselves and if we can improve that while keeping our defensive solidity, structure, desire and ultimately output, then we'll be a far better team."

articles.title: Max Verstappen vs Valentino Rossi: How their GT3 cars compare
articles.summary: The pair will race in the top-level Pro category during Saturday’s GT World Challenge Europe finale
articles.body:
Max Verstappen's Mercedes-AMG and Valentino Rossi's BMW is very different cars with a different number of turbos and a totally different soundtrack. But the rulebook is designed to make them equally fast. The two drivers will race this Saturday at Portimao in the final round of the GT World Challenge Europe Endurance Cup, but how do their weapons of choice compare?

It's a 61-car grid this weekend with Verstappen stepping in because regulars Jules Gounon and Daniel Juncadella are committed to the World Endurance Championship round at Barcelona. This means the Formula 1 ace and MotoGP legend will be going head to head in the top-level Pro category.

The Mercedes-AMG Team Verstappen Racing entry fields a Mercedes-AMG GT3 EVO with drivers Chris Lulham and Ben Barnicoat, managed on track by 2 Seas Motorsport. The team moved to Mercedes for 2026 after originally racing Aston Martins.

Powering the car is the M159, a naturally aspirated 6.3-litre V8 engine. The unit delivers approximately 550 horsepower, though power outputs adjust according to Balance of Performance regulations, which function to standardise performance across the GT3 category.

The layout is rear-wheel drive with a front-mid-mounted engine, a six-speed sequential gearbox and a weight of about 1,285kg, also set by BoP.

Rossi's No. 46 BMW M4 GT3 EVO, run by Team WRT, takes a different approach. Its P58 is a 3.0-litre (2,993cc) twin-turbo straight-six derived from the road car's engine, producing "up to 590hp" before BoP. It uses a six-speed Xtrac gearbox, measures 5,020mm long with splitter and wing on a 2,917mm wheelbase, and stops with 390mm front discs and six-piston calipers, plus 380mm discs at the rear. Rossi's co-drivers are BMW factory pair Max Hesse and Neil Verhagen.

Since its 2025 debut, the EVO has prioritised accessibility, durability, and cost-effectiveness over raw pace. The M4 GT3 has accumulated over 70 victories across its racing career, including victories at the 2023 Spa 24 Hours endurance race and the 2022 DTM championship.

On paper, then, the BMW has more power, but the BoP aims to neutralise that advantage, so neither car carries any advantage. Both vehicles employ front-mounted engines with rear-wheel drive and sequential transmissions, and they both employ 390mm front brakes. What really separates them is the engine note: a booming V8 versus a higher-pitched turbo six.

#46 Team WRT, BMW M4 GT3 EVO: Max Hesse, Valentino Rossi

Verstappen's GT3 record is short but impressive. Verstappen achieved victory in his debut race on 27 September 2025 at the Nurburgring NLS9 event, sharing a Ferrari 296 GT3 with Lulham and controlling the race from the opening lap to finish ahead by more than 20 seconds.

At the 2026 Nurburgring 24 Hours he led in the No. 3 Mercedes until a driveshaft failure struck with about three hours left. Sister car No. 80 went on to win - Mercedes' first victory there since 2016.

The 47-year-old Rossi, a nine-time motorcycle world champion, has competed in GT3 racing with Team WRT since 2022. Originally he drove Audis, but moved to BMW machinery from 2023 and has driven with the marque since.

His record includes three consecutive wins at the Misano Sprint, his home race, across 2023, 2024, and 2025, all achieved driving the M4. In addition to this, he scored multiple top-three finishes in the 2024 and 2025 LMGT3 seasons in the World Endurance Championship's GT3 category.

Rossi himself seems to know what he's up against. " Max Verstappen is going to be a huge problem because the bloke is just so incredibly fast," he said. With the machinery levelled by BoP, he's not wrong.

articles.title: 5 NHL Trade Landing Spots for Travis Konecny Amid NHL Rumors
articles.summary: The miserable start to the season for the Philadelphia Flyers has everyone looking for answers to find a way out. With an 0-5-3 record and already sporting a minus-21 goal differential, they need to get things right before it gets too far gone. Unfortunately, whenever there's a bad start, rumors start running wild and the latest one to pop up has to do with the team's leading scorer over the past few seasons, winger Travis Konecny.
articles.body:
The miserable start to the season for the Philadelphia Flyers has everyone looking for answers to find a way out. With an 0-5-3 record and already sporting a minus-21 goal differential, they need to get things right before it gets too far gone. Unfortunately, whenever there's a bad start, rumors start running wild and the latest one to pop up has to do with the team's leading scorer over the past few seasons, winger Travis Konecny.

Konecny was mentioned by Daily Faceoff as a player who is in an increasingly more difficult position and someone who could be traded to shake things up and provide the kind of return that could help alter the lineup in a positive way for Philly. There are some important hangups to doing that.

For one, Konecny has a full no-move clause, which means he has final say on any potential trade. Second, his contract has an $8.75 million salary cap hit and runs until 2033. Even though that price tag has become increasingly more affordable, it's not that easy to move. If the Flyers are going to attempt to run that gamut and make a brash move, we've come up with a list of teams who should be at the front of the line to try and make it happen.

As much as the Philadelphia Flyers were getting involved in trying to add to their roster over the summer, the other team that tried to knock on every door was the Montréal Canadiens. Picture those two teams working something out to produce a blockbuster trade that sent Travis Konecny to the Habs and what that would do to their already highly skilled team.

Adding Konecny to the Canadiens roster would allow them to bring in a natural replacement for the grit, feistiness and pure frustration that Brendan Gallagher provided for so many years there. Konecny's game is so similar to that of the former Habs fixture that making such a move is so obvious it hurts.

What would help make that kind of trade possible is how well equipped the Canadiens' prospect pipeline is to bring Philly to the table and they've got veterans who could be moved as well, an important thing since a Konecny trade would almost have to be a "hockey trade" to even get the Flyers to ask him to consider waiving his no-move protection.

Trading him within the Eastern Conference wouldn't be overly appealing for the Flyers, but Montréal's ability to sweeten any offer would make it difficult to pass up.

The Oilers are cooking to start the year and they're doing it without a few key players in the lineup like Zach Hyman and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins, not to mention goalie Frederik Andersen. But imagine if the Oilers wanted to really throw down the gauntlet and ruin everyone's Stanley Cup hopes in the West by adding Travis Konecny to the mix.

It would be a pure luxury splurge by the Oilers to make a run at Konecny and given how tight to the cap they are, it would take a really creative and potentially disruptive trade to make it happen. After all, Edmonton is about tapped out on prospects and carving veterans away from what's been a very good roster over the past few years may not be the kind of roster surgery GM Stan Bowman wants to do.

But when you think of what it would be like for the Oilers to matchup against Vegas, Anaheim, or any of the beastly teams in the Central Division with Konecny there to drive them nuts, it would be the kind of move that could finally bring the Cup back to Edmonton.

If there's a team that's meant to be watched if Travis Konecny becomes available, it's Carolina. GM Eric Tulsky has shown an eagerness to be involved, especially for top talent and with the amount of cap space they have, flexibility with the roster and prospects brewing in the pipeline, the Hurricanes can throw their weight around in trade talks.

The biggest hurdle in this case, of course, is the proximity. Carolina and Philly are both in the Metropolitan Division and there's no doubt the Flyers would hate to face Konecny four times a year in the regular season and certainly not in the playoffs.

The Hurricanes starting point for an offer would start with unsigned defenseman Alexander Nikishin and go from there and with Philly looking for defensive help, it's a good way to kick off negotiations. Desperate times can create funny trade partners sometimes and the Flyers and Hurricanes doing business after meeting in the playoffs a year ago would more than qualify.

Overreactions to the Start of the Season

The Mammoth are poised to be players in any trade market and with GM Bill Armstrong at the helm, they've been bold since moving to Salt Lake City. Watching Utah play, their speed and skill stand out but if you took that and added a bit of sandpaper with Travis Konecny, you'd have a team ready to bother everyone a lot worse in the West.

Utah's skill with Clayton Keller, Logan Cooley and Dylan Guenther are among the most fun groups in the league. When they added veteran leader Anders Lee to add some extra tenacity, it scratched an itch they were looking for in the lineup. Finding a way to add a player like Konecny and making use of the buildup of their prospect base to make it happen would elevate them more.

After all, Utah has prospects close to joining the NHL in Tij Iginla, Caleb Desnoyers, and 2026 first-round pick Ethan Belchetz along with other young guys who are there now in Daniil But and Dmitri Simashev. That's not to say that Philly would want to further their own rebuild-on-the-fly with younger players still, but if they were going to make a bold move like trading Konecny, adding elite high-end young talent would be appealing.

The Kings are in a bit of a funk to start the season themselves and getting bold and trying to add an agitating force like Travis Konecny would make sense.

Konecny's steady offensive production and ability to irritate opponents would play well in the Western Conference and particularly in a usually punchy Pacific Division battle for the playoffs. Should L.A. want to reinforce their attack on the wing, doing so with Konecny whose contract is settled and priced well for the future is good for them. As for what they could offer, well, that's up to GM Ken Holland to finagle.

There have been (and may still be) connections to Konecny from within the Kings organization from his days of junior hockey, so there are folks there that have known him a long time. The Kings and Flyers have also done a fair amount of business over the years, particularly in big trades, so linking them together has some historical basis.

articles.title: Dragons chasing home comforts in Challenge Cup
articles.summary: Dragons are looking to ensure knockout rugby at Rodney Parade this season as they prepare to start their Challenge Cup campaign against Perpignan.
articles.body:
Dragons will hunt home advantage in the knockout stages of the Challenge Cup after getting to the semi-finals the hard way last season.

Filo Tiatia's side start their European campaign with a fixture against Perpignan at Rodney Parade on Friday (20:00 BST).

Last season Dragons lost narrowly at eventual winners Montpellier in the semi-finals after winning away ties at Stade Francais and Zebre.

"It gave the team a lot of belief. We had to fight to get to the knockout stages and then we surprised a lot of people," said defence coach Dale MacLeod.

"We have had a taste of what it can be like and we are excited to have a French team coming to Rodney Parade."

In December they face South Africa's Cheetahs at Ospreys' redeveloped St Helen's ground before January fixtures against Bayonne in Newport and Ulster in Belfast.

With three games on Welsh soil before a tough Irish trip, Dragons not only have the chance to take a big step towards qualification but also knock-out rugby at Rodney Parade.

There were 28 knockout fixtures played with home advantage in last season's Champions and Challenge Cups, with just six won by the away team.

"Your own crowd and support, the ease of just getting into your car and driving to the ground, all of those things make a difference in the performance," said MacLeod.

"Last year we had to fly back from playing in the URC in South Africa, then fly to France to play Stade Francais, come back to the UK and then out to Parma.

"If you can get a home run then all that stuff is so much easier."

Dragons have not hosted a European knockout tie since losing to Northampton in the last 16 of the Challenge Cup in 2021, when the fixture was played behind closed doors because of the Covid pandemic.

Their last knockout game in front of fans in Newport was the 2015 quarter-final victory against Cardiff.

Dragons started the season with a draw at Benetton and a win against Scarlets, but lost a topsy-turvy home derby with Ospreys last weekend.

Tiatia makes seven changes this weekend with in-form Wales wing Rio Dyer bringing up a century of appearances.

Props Rodrigo Martinez, Chris Coleman and Rob Hunt area missing because of injury, so there is a new-look front row of Rhodri Jones, Brodie Coghlan and Owain James.

Wales tight-head Dillon Lewis returns to the replacements bench, while lock Barny Langton-Cryer partners captain Ben Carter. Fellow co-captain Angus O'Brien is missing with a minor injury.

Fly-half Jac Lloyd is given only his second start for the club with Tinus de Beer switching to full-back, while wing Jared Rosser makes his first start of the season.

Perpignan have won their three home games in the Top 14 this season but have lost all three on their travels.

The French side won 41-17 when the teams met at Stade Aime Giral in December 2025.

"They are big, physical and flamboyant. Give them a sniff by letting them into the 22 and they will kick the door down and truck over," said MacLeod.

"They are big men, and skilful. If they are on top then they express themselves and they are a dangerous side."

The fixture will feature the new European try-bonus rule.

Scoring four tries no longer guarantees an extra point - teams must score at least three more than their opponents.

Dragons: De Beer; Dyer, Inisi, Owen, J Rosser; J Lloyd, Hope; R Jones, Coghlan, O James, Langton-Cryer, Carter (capt), Lewis-Hughes, Beddall, Keddie.

Replacements: Dee, W Jones, Lewis, Screech, Minto, R Williams, F Paea, Tuitavuki.

Perpignan: Tedder; Toganiyadrava, Reece, de la Fuente (capt), Granell; McIntyre, McGrath; Boyer-Gallardo, Malolo, Riccioni, Chinarro, Tanguy, J van Tonder, Coulon, Dvali.

Replacements: Lotrian, Tetrashvili, Amituanai, Velarte, Taty, Tuilagi, Aucagne, Mascarenc.

Referee: Hanru van Rooyen (South Africa)

Assistant referees : Alex Thomas (England), Hamish Grant (England)
